title: Centre a microscope slide's alignment cross and focus it sharply with the stage and focus knobs
instruction: Centre the crossing of the slide's two scales in the microscope's field of view and focus it sharply; the camera image is on the monitor.
context: This task tests the positioning and focusing step used to prepare microscope images for calibrated measurements in laboratory research. A preloaded stage micrometer provides a repeatable target; the robot uses stage and coarse/fine focus knobs to centre its crossed scales and bring their graduations into sharp focus on the camera monitor. CDC's ocular-micrometer job aid instructs focusing a stage-micrometer scale, and Evident's camera-calibration guide uses an object micrometer with a focused system. The task covers physical preparation, not calculating a calibration factor. Full credit needs the crossing within 0.05 mm of the image centre in a 0.38 x 0.22 mm field and focus within 5 um. Closest accepted look-alike: TK-UJB387 registers a workpiece against a corner stop; here centring and focusing use a magnified image and stage/focus controls.
setup: Station table (top 0.7475 m). Robot base frame: x forward, y to the robots' left. Upright microscope, fixed, representing the named trial configuration (AmScope VB-B110C binocular microscope with 1 MP USB eyepiece camera, about $411 to $424: B110C stand with 50 x 25 mm 2-layer mechanical stage, coaxial coarse/fine focus with 2 um fine divisions, 10x/0.25 objective and bottom LED light, plus MD100-class camera; MAGUS CS5 slide, about $43 to $48; printed stage-knob belt adapter in adapter/, about $24 to $34 checkout / $18 to $26 consumed; dedicated parts total about $478 to $506, README), facing the robots, centred at (0.34, 0.06): white stand with a 26 x 16 cm base, a pillar at the back and an arm (6 cm wide) over the stage carrying the binocular head, swivelled to face away from the robots (eyepieces inclined 45 degrees up and back, the eyepiece camera in the one on the robots' left) and a steel 10x objective (24 mm across) on the axis (0.31, 0.06), front lens 12 cm above the table. Mechanical stage: dark plates (10 x 13 cm on top) that move up and down with the focus knobs and in x and y with the stage knobs; it travels 25 mm towards and away from the robots and 50 mm left to right, and starts at its limits 12.5 mm towards the robots and 25 mm to the left, 1 mm below focus. Slide holder on the stage: two back posts and a left stop, and a steel L-lever pivoting behind the slide's right end, its jaw across that end and its 6 cm handle out to the right with a black post at the end; a light spring holds it closed on the slide. Stage knobs (15 mm of stage travel per turn in the model from rough one-turn ruler measurements on a Zeiss Axio Imager.A2 reference stand; B110C leads and adapter mounting dimensions are unmeasured assumptions qualified before trials, README): the two black ribbed top knobs, 34 mm across and 97 mm apart, of the printed belt adapter on the lower stage plate's right edge: inner one (x) at (0.205, -0.046), outer one (y) at (0.205, -0.144), tops 17.5 mm above the stage top; each turns one coaxial stage knob under the stage 1:1 by a belt; they rise with the stage. Light: the bottom LED's spot, 24 mm across, on the objective's axis under the slide. Focus: one shaft through a housing under the stage, with a black ribbed coarse knob 4.2 cm across on each side (axis 7 cm above the table at x = 0.30; 2 mm per turn in the model from the Zeiss manual) and, outboard of each, a fine knob 2.6 cm across (0.2 mm per turn in the model). Slide, loaded in the holder, label on the left: a glass calibration slide (MAGUS CS5, about $43 to $48), 76 x 26 mm (drawn 2 mm thick), its two 1 mm scales (0.01 mm divisions) crossing at its centre, which starts 12.5 mm in front of and 25.5 mm left of the axis. Camera monitor, fixed: a black tablet 19.2 x 11.4 x 1.2 cm lying flat on the table between the robots at (0.09, 0), screen up, showing the camera's live 10x view over its whole 18 x 10.2 cm screen: the eyepiece camera sees 0.38 x 0.22 mm of the slide (0.38 mm left to right; 469 mm on the screen per mm), its centre on the objective's axis: bright over the glass; the two scale lines move with the stage (away from the robots is towards the screen's far edge), are drawn across the whole screen with their 0.01 mm ticks (4.7 mm apart on the screen) while their crossing is on it, sharp within 5 um of focus, soft within 0.1 mm, blurred within 1 mm, and are lost in the blur beyond.
scoring: Measured once everything has come to rest. 0 unless the slide is still in the holder: flat (tilt up to 3 degrees) with its centre within 3 mm of the holder's centre, label on the left, the holder's jaw closed. 0 also if the slide came within 0.5 mm of the objective at any time. Every positive score also needs both hands released: all six jaw and pad points at least 80 mm from every microscope, slide, holder, knob and monitor surface; and all moving task parts, including the holder and the control knobs, moved less than 1 mm over the final 21 samples at 20 Hz (1.0 s). Then: 0 unless the scales' crossing is in the camera's 0.38 x 0.22 mm view (within 0.19 mm left to right and 0.11 mm towards or away from the objective's axis); 0.5 if it is; 0.75 if the slide's top is also within 0.1 mm of focus (5.2 mm below the front lens); 1.0 if within 5 um of focus (the 10x / 0.25 objective's depth of field is about 10 um) and the crossing within 0.05 mm of the axis (the image centre). Possible scores: 0, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. Real trial: the crossing's offset is read on the monitor with the camera software's centre crosshair against the slide's own 0.01 mm divisions; the focus error is the fine-knob travel to the scales' best focus, read off its 2 um graduations; two synchronized videos with a tape scale show the hands' release and clearance, the still final second and the smallest gap between the slide and the front lens.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Lower the stage 1 mm below focus, drive it to its front-left limits (12.5 mm towards the robots, 25 mm left), and leave the slide in the holder, label on the left, the jaw closed.
fidelity: Rigid bodies in PhysX at 240 Hz. Knobs turn on damped hinges; stiff drives move the stage. Simulated leads follow a Zeiss A2 reference stand: x and y 15 mm/turn (rough ruler check), coarse 2 and fine 0.2 mm/turn (Zeiss manual). VB-B110C leads, 5.2 mm working distance and adapter knob defaults are assumed pending pre-trial qualification. Slide drawn 2 mm thick (real 1.1 mm). No optics: position-based monitor view with stepped blur; stage z scores focus.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (4,800 steps); demo: 1.0 (3,831 of 4,800 steps, 191.6 s, at the simulated 15/2/0.2 mm/turn reference gearing)
